title: StateTradeRecord
description: One record = one (state, trade) pair. It is the unit the rules engine loads, the unit the expansion playbook renders, and the unit the drift cron re-verifies. Launch scope (PLAN.md A11) is 3 trades x 15 states = 45 records.

record_id.description: Grammar: <state_code_lower>.<trade>. Append-only, never renamed; see ontology/id-grammar.md.

jurisdiction_model.description: The single most important field in the record and the one every competitor gets wrong. It answers: is there a state licence at all, or does the contractor need a city or county licence in every jurisdiction they pull a permit in?

local_layer_note.description: Free text describing what the local layer adds. Never a list of specific municipalities unless each is separately sourced.

boards.description: More than one where the state splits the trade across agencies (NC splits electrical from plumbing/heating; Texas splits plumbing from everything else).

phone.description: Organisation switchboard only. Never a named individual (phase-3 standing rule).

level.description: The normalised rung. This is what makes 45 states comparable: a Texas 'Responsible Master Plumber' and a Florida 'Certified Plumbing Contractor' both map to a rung, so the roster UI and the alert engine do not need per-state code.

expiry_rule.description: How the expiry DATE is computed, not the date itself. Three shapes appear in the launch scope and the rules engine must handle all three: 'anniversary' (TX: one year from issue), 'fixed_date' (NC: 31 December every year), 'fixed_date_parity' (FL: 31 August of even years for certified, odd for registered). The value string is one of those tokens plus its parameters.

period.description: The window the hours must fall inside, in months, and whether it is tied to the licence term or to a calendar.

subject_breakdown.description: array of {hours, subject} where the state mandates specific subjects. Florida's 14 hours are six separate mandates; a customer who takes 14 general hours still fails.

delivery_constraint.description: e.g. NC electrical: at least half the hours must be in-person classroom.

financial_responsibility.description: Florida's credit-score gate lives here; it is not insurance, but it is the same class of pre-condition and the buyer meets it in the same breath.

reciprocity.description: Empty array is a meaningful, publishable answer ('this board has no reciprocity agreements') ONLY when reciprocity_statement below carries a source that says so. An empty array with no statement fails the validator.

direction.description: inbound = a holder of the other state's licence can obtain this state's licence. Direction is asymmetric far more often than contractors expect and is where the expansion playbook earns its fee.

requires_from.description: The other state's licence that must be held.

qualifying_individual_rule.description: Who the company must employ for the company to hold a licence, and whether that person may qualify more than one company. This is the field that turns a roll-up's acquisition into a licensing emergency.

change_notification_deadline.description: How long the company has to name a replacement when the qualifier leaves. Texas electrical: 30 business days. This is an alertable deadline and belongs in the same engine as renewals.

publishable.description: The gate. False until pass_a and pass_b agree on every value whose status is 'verified'. The app loads only publishable records; the rest are visible to admin only.

coverage_notes.description: What this record deliberately does NOT cover yet, in the buyer's words. Rendered verbatim at the foot of any playbook built from the record. A gap the customer can see is a gap that does not become a refund.
